title: ADR-05 Versioned state, taint, write-write conflict rule, deduped re-run (FIRST PRIORITY)
outcome: Own row-versioned SQLite (obj=table:pk, get→(value, ver, author), history), conservative forward/backward taint, recovery plan C5 with dry-run diff; due 23 Nov so build starts day 1
acceptance: ADR file ≤900 words with sections Context, Decision, Consequences, Interface touched (which of C1–C6), Tests that prove it
Write-write rule: restore only if current ver == culprit's after-version, else re-run or flag; recovery appends compensating records, never edits history
Re-runs of deterministic steps go through the outbox deduped by idempotency key (re-emitted effects = 0); LLM steps become a replan item for console approval; coarse/aggregate reads over-taint
Tests listed cover the F2+ triage conflict row, a re-run that would re-fire payment/email, and backward taint naming root candidates
summary: ADR-05 written (898 words). Own SQLite: objects (live heads) plus append-only versions (obj, ver, hash, author, seq, action_id), with history values kept in the side store. Maya's ver and seq conventions are confirmed, with three amendments: tombstones continue the counter; a restore creates a new version and taint keys on (obj, ver) not hash; a version is visible only after its seq. Forward taint comes from recorded read sets only. The default is conservative: aggregate reads over-taint and an LLM agent stays tainted after it reads a tainted version. Backward taint ranks root candidates by earliest causal write, then by descendants. Plan order: cancel_outbox, then restore only if the head is still the culprit's after-version (otherwise flag write_write_conflict), then a deterministic rerun through the outbox. The rerun dedupes on idempotency_key: a held item is superseded in place; a dispatched item emits nothing and is flagged. Then compensate (C), replan (LLM), and I2/dispatched effects go to the report. Each step is a signed ks.recover envelope and is re-checked in the transaction: tamper gives FROZEN; a stale expect gives hold/needs_approval. Tests: triage conflict, no double payment (hold 0 and >0, double apply), root candidates (RT9), conservative taint, append-only/fold, frozen, golden plan. No contract field change. Optional ask: a stale_plan hold reason.
review:
[maya · changes] CHANGES (maya). The store (§1-2) is approved, so build of ks.state can start day 1. Amendments (a)-(c) are accepted and fit the WriteEntry validator; I fold them into the C3 docs (CON-02 M11). The write-write rule, append-only recovery, idempotency-key dedupe, conservative taint, the FROZEN re-check and the golden plan all meet the acceptance criteria. stale_plan is ACCEPTED: Reason.STALE_PLAN under HOLD (M8). Use hold/stale_plan, not needs_approval. Fix these by 23 Nov:
1. AGENT VIEW (blocker, shared with me). Agents decide on data that never enters a read set. Example: crm applies ticket T-3, but its crm.update_supplier record reads only suppliers:SUP. Forward taint then under-taints and RT9 backward taint never reaches intake. I'm proposing a gateway-captured TickFrame.view whose entries join that tick's record read_set (CON-02 M6). Your §3 must state the rule, and a test must prove crm's record carries tickets:T-3.
2. §4 ranking must match ADR-04: rank 0 = the writer of evidence_versions (write_set lookup), then backward-taint candidates. Bound the walk, or give a secondary order, so the oldest ancestor (seed data) doesn't rank first. Add a test where crm's read set also holds an older supplier version written by a third agent, and intake is still in the top 3.
3. test_root_candidates contradicts ADR-06/SPEC RT9: comms doesn't write suppliers. Use intake plants T-3, crm writes the IBAN, expected [crm, intake], inventory and docs absent.
4. HERO R (decide explicitly). The object is a row, so the flagged S-17 v3 still carries the swapped IBAN, and F2+ scores R>0 against the D13 target R=0. Either (A) keep the flag and state that the hero R covers flagged rows only (tell zoya/tara), or (B), my recommendation and allowed by "else re-run": when every version above `to` is tainted and every writer above the culprit is a deterministic honest action, restore with expect = the current tainted head and re-run triage. Flag only when the head writer is an LLM or non-deterministic. Untainted heads are kept, as now (M13).
5. Rerun mechanics: it re-executes the original tool and args (side store) for ActionRef.agent_id/action_id. Keys derive from those, OutboxItem.author stays the original agent, and redacted args become a flag (M14). "Re-enters the hold" means: status queued, release_tick = tick + hold_window_ticks, lineage = the rerun's recorded read set.
6. Dry-run: the diff for re-runs needs simulation in a rolled-back savepoint. replan objects get no DiffEntry. dispatched_tainted is decided from the simulated payload hash.
7. Apply halts at the first stale step. Steps already applied stay (append-only), and the console gets a new plan with as_of_seq = now.
8. ks.recover.<op> must be in the ADR-03 catalogue for principal ks.recovery, or it is denied as class U (with nisha; SEC-03 F2). Say which ops create envelopes: flag and replan create none, they are report/console only. Bind steps to an approval record (SEC-03 F5).
9. FROZEN also when verify != OK, so a dead-dir edit freezes too (RT7); it lasts for the rest of the run (M12).
10. t0_seq is the planner's estimate and must never read RunConfig.fault_tick/culprit (scorer-only).
Keep it ≤900 words (currently 898): move test detail to the test file.
